samples.summary: Canonical design doc not updated for the new `data-text-edit-keepalive` exemption. The doc's "It deliberately does nothing when" list (lines 147-160) is the spec for this hook and is now incomplete; worse, its last bullet asserts text-edit controls are handled purely by the deferred activeElement re-read ("which is what makes text-edit controls … no-ops"), which the delta contradicts by adding an explicit keepalive special case in `toolbar-focus-release.ts:76`. CONTRIBUTING expects the behaviour change to be folded into the canonical subsystem doc.

Design doc is now factually stale about board: it states "Board carries its own copy of the same `<button>` branch …; the attribute is opt-in, so the board toolbar can adopt the hook when that surface is verified" (162-165) and that the hook is "called by the desktop slides toolbar" (143). The delta makes the board toolbar a second caller (`board-toolbar.tsx:137,186`) without updating either sentence, and nothing is recorded in `docs/design/board/board-editing-parity.md` either.

Scope creep vs the task's stated deferral. `docs/tasks/active/20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md` Out-of-scope (lines 49-55) says the board case is a pointer only and "the new attribute is opt-in, so board can adopt the hook later without touching this change"; the task list (39-47) covers only the slides toolbar. This delta adopts board anyway, and the todo's task list/out-of-scope section was not amended to reflect it.

The keepalive exemption partially walks back the issue's acceptance criterion for the controls it covers. Per the recorded design (todo line 33-35, lessons lines 25-29) the deferred `document.activeElement` re-read already makes text-edit controls no-ops, so the exemption is either redundant or, in the cases where focus genuinely remains parked on a keepalive `<button>` (Clear formatting, alignment trigger, colour swatches in the slides text-edit section), it re-creates exactly the #882 symptom: the document-level gate stays engaged for that button, so after the text session ends the canvas needs another click. Worth confirming which of the two it is before merging, since the goal statement is "the canvas is the keyboard target again … without needing another canvas click".

The new doc comment's claim that the exemption "is also what lets the shared pickers keep their documented 'dismiss restores focus to the trigger' contract" does not match `components/menu-focus.ts:10-29`, which documents the opposite intent for slides ("slides: anywhere but the trigger `<button>`") and says outside-click/Esc simply fall through to Radix then the natural click target/body. Rationale in the shared module and in this hook should not disagree.

`data-text-edit-keepalive` is now hard-coded in a fourth place (docs `text-box-editor.ts:748`, ~16 JSX call sites, and now this selector) even though the module right beside it exports `CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR` as a named constant for exactly this reason; an archived lessons doc already flagged the duplicated magic string. Cross-package sharing may be impossible, but a frontend-side exported constant is not.

Slides deliberately scoped the hook to the desktop toolbar (todo Out-of-scope: "The mobile slides toolbar (bottom sheets, no hardware keyboard target)"), gating the call before its `isMobile` branch is irrelevant because only the desktop `<Toolbar>` carries the attribute. `BoardToolbar` has no mobile variant (board-editing-parity.md lists "Mobile board toolbar" as a non-goal), so the board now applies the release on touch surfaces too — a small, undiscussed divergence from the slides scoping decision.

verdict.reason: The exemption is present as quoted, but neither prong of the finding holds. (1) Not redundant: `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751` skips the blur-commit only when focus lands in `[data-text-edit-keepalive]`, so a match means the text session is still live, and `menu-focus.ts:19-29` plus `text-paragraph-group.tsx:94-101` record the "Esc/outside-click restores focus to the trigger" contract — removing the exemption would blur that trigger and re-arm canvas Delete/type-to-edit against a mounted text box. (2) It cannot re-create #882: every keepalive-tagged control inside a `data-canvas-toolbar` root is rendered only by `TextEditSection` (`app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110,136-138`, `text-edit-section.tsx:63-105`), which is mounted only while `state.kind === "text-edit"` (`index.tsx:85`). When the session ends those controls unmount, so focus cannot remain parked on one afterwards, and the object/idle controls the acceptance criterion targets (`object-section.tsx`, arrange menu, zoom, slide group) carry no keepalive attribute and are released normally. The only real residue is that the design doc bullet list (`docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:147-160`) and the lessons note omit the guard — doc-completeness, minor, non-blocking.
